# CROSS-TIER PATHS — frontend files that BACKEND tests read off disk.
#
# #5007 (THRU-H). The change classifier may drop the backend jobs for a
# frontend-only candidate. That is only safe because the backend suite is
# assumed not to depend on `frontend/`. It does: twelve backend test files are
# cross-tier parity guards that read client source and assert the client
# consumes what the backend serves.
#
# A frontend-only change that touches ANY path below therefore still runs the
# full suite. Touching none of them is what makes "frontend-only" mean
# "no backend test can see this".
#
# THIS FILE IS NOT MAINTAINED BY HAND ALONE. `backend/tests/test_ci_cross_tier_manifest.py`
# re-derives the set from `backend/tests/` on every run and goes red when a new
# cross-tier read appears that is not listed here. Without that guard this list
# rots into a fail-open the first time somebody adds a parity test — which is
# the whole risk of the classifier, so the guard is the load-bearing half, not
# the list.
#
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. One repo-relative path per line.
#
# A line ending in `/` is a DIRECTORY PREFIX and covers everything beneath it.
# `test_playoff_degraded_contract.py` builds a fixtures directory and then joins
# filenames onto it, so no file-level entry can honestly describe what it reads —
# the directory is the real dependency.

frontend/lib/marketShape.ts
frontend/app/sports/page.tsx
frontend/lib/discover/feedPaging.ts
frontend/lib/tournamentHubs.ts
frontend/components/discover/utils.ts
frontend/app/playoffs/[sport]/page.tsx
frontend/e2e/helpers/sweepFiling.js
frontend/e2e/scripts/file-sweep-findings.js
frontend/lib/discover/feedFreshness.ts
frontend/components/futures/OutcomeRow.tsx
frontend/components/weather/data.ts

# Named as WHOLE-PATH literals rather than component chains (CERT-2566). The
# first cut of the scanner could not see this shape, so these three were missing
# and a change to any of them was classified `frontend` while a backend contract
# depended on it.
frontend/__tests__/components/tournamentReskin.test.tsx
frontend/lib/discoverInteractions.ts
frontend/lib/play/session.ts
frontend/__tests__/fixtures/

# Arrived AFTER this guard did, which is the case the guard exists for. #3179's
# branch was gated green on 2026-09-09 and merged on 2026-09-12; the manifest and
# its rot guard landed between the two (2026-09-10). Exact-sha CI is immutable, so
# a token cannot notice that master grew a new census under it — only a re-run at
# the merge base can, and only the guard makes that re-run say anything. The read
# is real: `test_client_timing_contract.py` parses `PERF_EVENT_KEYS` out of
# `sanitize.ts` so the server allowlist and the browser's cannot drift, which is
# exactly a frontend-only edit that can redden a backend shard.
frontend/lib/analytics/sanitize.ts

# #6219. `test_card_names_an_outcome_it_draws_6219.py` reads the
# `leaderFirstSlice(distributionRows, 4)` literal out of this component, because
# the number of rows the card DRAWS is what decides whether a movement sentence
# may name its subject. The backend's `CARD_DRAWN_OUTCOME_ROWS` and this literal
# are two records of one capability, and the guard asserts the gap rather than
# trusting it. That guard is only worth having if it RUNS on the change that can
# break it — a frontend-only edit widening the slice to five would otherwise be
# classified `frontend`, skip this shard, and silently leave the backend
# suppressing sentences about rows the reader can now see.
frontend/components/discover/FuturesCard.tsx

# #6381. `test_venue_settled_payload_6381.py` reads `hasNoReportedResult` out of
# this file and asserts it still has exactly the two arms the server's
# `venue_settlement_is_askable` mirrors. "No result reported" is defined HERE and
# nowhere else; the backend gate decides which rows get told the venue already
# graded them, so the day the web side grows a third way to say the sentence, the
# server ships #6381's fix to a subset of its own class and nothing says so.
# That guard is worth having only if it RUNS on the change that breaks it — and
# adding an arm to this file is precisely the frontend-only edit that would
# otherwise be classified `frontend` and skip the shard that holds it.
frontend/lib/eventState.ts

# #5657. `test_sport_display_name_never_serves_raw_key_5657.py` parses the family
# words out of `getLeagueDisplay` in this file, because #5657 gives the server a
# name for the 15 `*_other` rows and the word it serves must be the word web
# already derives from the key — otherwise one payload reads "Other Baseball" on
# the web and something else in the app, which is the two-tier disagreement the
# ship exists to end. The guard READS web's table rather than restating it, so
# it can notice a rename; that is only true if it RUNS on the rename. Renaming a
# family here is exactly the frontend-only edit that would otherwise be
# classified `frontend`, skip this shard, and let the two tiers drift apart
# silently — with the server now the one asserting the stale word.
frontend/lib/sportCategories.ts

# #6238. `test_event_payload_draw_priced_away_6238.py` reads the ONE
# `winnerMarketPricesADraw: true` row out of this file's `SPORT_SCORING` table
# and asserts it is character-for-character the server's
# `DRAW_PRICED_SPORT_KEY_MATCHES`. Three runtimes decide whether a sport's
# winner market prices a draw — server, web and Swift — and they must decide it
# the same way or one withholds the away figure where another prints a
# complement, which is the exact split that let the web print `1 - home` for
# five days after native stopped. Widening the rule to a second sport is a
# one-word edit HERE, and it is precisely the frontend-only change the
# classifier would send past the shard holding the parity test: the server would
# keep serving a fabricated away on a sport the web had already declared
# three-way, and nothing would say so.
frontend/lib/marketMapUtils.ts
